topic: Show depth-first search on a tree-shaped graph from A
title: Depth-First Search and Backtracking

scenes.narration: Depth first search follows one path as far as it can, then backs up to the last node that still has somewhere new to go. A stack holds the path we are on. We start at A and take neighbours in alphabetical order.
scenes.caption: Go deep, then back up

scenes.narration: We visit A and put it on the stack. The current node is A.
scenes.caption: visit A

scenes.narration: A's first unvisited neighbour is B, so we go deeper to B and push it. The top of the stack is B.
scenes.caption: A to B

scenes.narration: From B we go on to D. The stack now holds the whole path: A, B, D.
scenes.caption: B to D

scenes.narration: D has nowhere new to go, so we pop it and back up to B. B still has E, so we visit E next.
scenes.caption: back to B, then E

scenes.narration: E is a dead end and so is B now. We pop both and back up to A, whose next neighbour is C.
scenes.caption: back to A, then C

scenes.narration: From C we reach F. Every node has been visited, in the order A, B, D, E, C, F.
scenes.caption: C to F

scenes.narration: The stack is the same as the call stack of a recursive search. Depth first search finds paths, connected parts and cycles, and it is the base of topological sorting.
scenes.caption: Summary
points: Follow one path as deep as it goes
A stack remembers the way back
Visits every reachable node in O(V + E)

quiz.question: A graph has edges A-B, A-C and B-D. Depth first search from A takes four steps. In what order are the nodes visited?
quiz.explanation: From B the search goes deeper to D before it backs up to C.

quiz.question: A graph has edges A-B, B-C and A-D. After three depth first steps from A, which node is on top of the stack?
quiz.explanation: The path is A, B, C, so C is on top.
